//: The page has always been served straight out of src/ with no build. It is
built now: src/*.ts is compiled to dist/*.js, and dist is what the browser
loads. Every module in src/ is TypeScript; the move is done.
Imports still name .js — './noise.js', not './noise.ts'. That is not a
leftover. tsc never rewrites a module specifier, and dist/ is loaded by the
browser as plain ES modules, so a specifier has to name the file that will
be fetched. '.ts' is rejected outright; bare './noise' would compile under
moduleResolution bundler and then fail to resolve in the browser.
allowJs and checkJs are what made the move survivable one file at a time: a
module not yet renamed still compiled and still landed in dist/, so the page
kept working with forty .js files and one .ts, and none of them was type-
checked while it waited its turn. Nothing in src/ is .js any more, so both
are no-ops today and can go whenever.
three is a devDependency for its types alone. At runtime it still comes
from the CDN through the import map in index.html, which is why the paths
below point three/addons/* at the same examples/jsm the import map does.
